back: An RNA virus that uses reverse transcriptase to make DNA from its RNA in the host cell.
Two RNA strands, reverse transcriptase, integrase, protease, protein capsid, lipid envelope with glycoproteins (gp120).
It destroys T-helper cells, so B-cells and T-killer cells are not activated and opportunistic infections develop.

front: CD4 count at which AIDS is diagnosed
back: Below about 200 cells per mm³ (healthy adults about 500-1,500).
Unprotected sex, infected blood (needles, transfusion), mother to child (pregnancy, birth, breastfeeding).
Drugs inhibit reverse transcriptase, integrase or protease, so replication stops, viral load falls and CD4 count recovers.
Pre-exposure prophylaxis: HIV-negative people take antiretroviral drugs to prevent infection.
An infection that causes serious disease only when immunity is weakened, e.g. TB, oral thrush.
Viral DNA is integrated into host chromosomes as a provirus in long-lived cells.
